title: BBQ Chicken Pizza
subtitle: Sweet BBQ, red onion, cilantro
description: Sweet BBQ, red onion, cilantro. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for BBQ Chicken Pizza in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Season and toss the chicken
steps.instruction: Toss shredded chicken with half the BBQ sauce, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Taste — sauce should be bold because cheese mellows it. Keep remaining sauce for the line.

steps.title: Heat oven and stone or steel
steps.instruction: Place a pizza stone or inverted sheet pan in the oven. Preheat to 500°F at least 40 minutes. Shred cheese and slice red onion while the oven saturates — surface temp matters more than air temp.

steps.title: Stretch dough and oil rims
steps.instruction: On a floured surface, stretch each dough ball to a 12–14 inch round. Leave a ½ inch rim. Brush rims lightly with olive oil so edges brown. Work on parchment dusted with cornmeal so pies slide on the peel.

steps.title: Sauce, cheese, chicken, onion
steps.instruction: Spread a thin ring of BBQ sauce on each crust — less than tomato night; sweet sauce pools in the center. Layer mozzarella and gouda, then chicken and red onion. Do not overload wet chicken or the center sags.

steps.title: Bake until edges char
steps.instruction: Bake each pie 10–13 minutes until cheese bubbles with brown spots and the bottom sounds hollow when tapped. Rotate once for hot spots. Hold finished pies on racks, not stacked — steam kills crust.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion BBQ Chicken Pizza onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Rest, cilantro, and cut
steps.instruction: Rest 2 minutes so cheese sets. Drizzle remaining BBQ sauce in thin ribbons and scatter cilantro. Cut into 8 slices per pie and fan on sheet trays for eight hungry firefighters. Backup pie holds at 200°F uncovered up to 15 minutes.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up BBQ Chicken Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sweet BBQ, red onion, cilantro. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — BBQ Chicken Pizza runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
